issues.where: data/public/dossiers/math-tutoring-econ/prior_project.md §4.2: “Students who attended at least 80% of sessions ... showed a larger effect ... 0.27 SD (95% CI [0.13, 0.41])”; dossier.yaml F27.
issues.problem: Attendance is measured after school randomisation. Selecting high attenders breaks the randomised comparison, yet this is presented as a larger treatment effect without a comparator, identification method or selection-bias caveat. The methods only describe the ITT model. An applicant can therefore repeat a misleading causal dose-response claim while faithfully following the dossier.
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: “In an exploratory comparison of the 1,614 treatment students attending at least 80% of sessions with the control sample, the adjusted difference was 0.27 SD (95% CI [0.13, 0.41]). Attendance was not randomised; this selected-sample association does not identify a causal effect of higher attendance or establish an effect larger than the ITT estimate.” Mirror this qualification in F27 and register it as a salient limitation. Keep the numerical result and primary ITT result unchanged.
